small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_P (e.g. 32, 64) at BLOCK_OC=32/64 so each program covers more pool windows and amortizes weight loads; current BLOCK_P=16 means TILE=256 but weight reuse across pools is the main lever.
- Try BLOCK_OC=128 with BLOCK_P=16/32 and num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 to better hide the conv-MAC latency over IC*KH*KW=72 inner iterations.
- Hoist weight loads out of the spatial loop: load the full (BLOCK_OC, IC*KH*KW) weight tile once per program into registers/shared (via a 2D `tl.load`), then reuse across all pool windows — currently weights are re-loaded for every (kh,kw,ic) inside the spatial tile, wasting bandwidth.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an explicit im2col-style GEMM: one program computes a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_P*POOL*POOL) output tile via `tl.dot` over the K=IC*KH*KW axis. This uses tensor cores instead of the current scalar outer-product accumulation, which is the main reason the kernel sits at ~0.82x — RTX 4090 mma throughput dominates fp32 FMA here.
- Use channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous in memory; pre-permute x once per forward (cheap relative to conv) and load K-vectors with coalesced reads.
- Keep the tanh→scale→bias→maxpool epilogue fused on the accumulator in registers, but reshape the (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_P, POOL*POOL) view after the dot and reduce with `tl.max` exactly as now. Consider one program per (N, OC-tile) persistent over all pool tiles to amortize weight loads across the entire output spatial grid.
